title: Total solar eclipse Aug. 12, 2026 live updates — 3 days to totality
summary: Follow our live coverage of the total solar eclipse 2026 as we count down to eclipse day with the latest news, expert insight and updates before bringing you live reports from Greenland and Spain.
contentText:
On Aug. 12, 2026, Europe will experience its first total solar eclipse since 1999, as the moon's shadow sweeps across Greenland, Iceland, northern Spain and the Balearic Islands.

Along the narrow path of totality, day will briefly turn to twilight as the moon completely covers the sun, revealing its elusive outer atmosphere — the corona. Meanwhile, millions more skywatchers across much of Europe, as well as parts of northeastern United States and eastern Canada, will witness a partial solar eclipse as the moon appears to take a bite out of the sun.

Live reporting from the path of totality

We'll be following the eclipse from two locations along the path of totality.

Our skywatching editor Daisy Dobrijevic is currently aboard HX Expeditions ' MS Spitsbergen exploring Greenland's dramatic coast. She'll be aiming to witness totality from Scoresby Sund, the world's largest and longest fjord system. Dobrijevic is hoping for more eclipse luck than last time, when unfortunately, totality was a total bust , but not for the reason you may think.

Meanwhile, our skywatching writer Anthony Wood is joining the DEB initiative in Valoria la Buena, Spain, where the eclipsed sun will hang low above the western horizon shortly before sunset. It will be Wood's first-ever total solar eclipse .

One week until the total solar eclipse 2026: The countdown has begun... are you ready?

The countdown has begun! The total solar eclipse 2026 will occur on Aug. 12. (Image credit: Photo by Erin Clark/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) In just one week, millions of people across Greenland, Iceland and Spain will witness one of nature's greatest spectacles as the moon completely covers the sun.

Our team will be following the eclipse from two incredible locations, aboard an expedition ship in East Greenland with HX Expeditions and from northern Spain with the DEB initiative , bringing you live updates throughout the lead-up to the eclipse and on the day itself

August 5, 2026 – 1:08 PM Last call for eclipse glasses!

Eclipse glasses must be worn whenever the sun's disk is visible. (Image credit: LeoPatrizi / Getty Images) If you're planning on viewing the Aug. 12 total solar eclipse then you'll need to get hold of a pair of quality eclipse glasses. Be sure to get a pair from a reputable dealer that conforms to the all important ISO 123-12 - 2 certification and never use an old pair if they appear scratched or damaged in any way!

August 6, 2026 – 5:03 AM Where will the eclipse be visible?

Find out where you can experience totality on Aug. 12, 2026. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Not everyone will experience totality on Aug. 12.

Some places will see the moon completely cover the sun, while others will experience a partial solar eclipse and for some… no eclipse at all. Womp womp.

August 7, 2026 – 4:39 AM Do clouds ruin a total solar eclipse?

Clouds won't necessarily sour your eclipse expedition. (Image credit: Vaughn Ridley/Getty Images) One of the biggest worries before any eclipse is weather.

While a perfectly blue sky is ideal, you don't necessarily need one to enjoy the experience. Even under thin clouds, many of the most dramatic effects of totality can still be visible.

August 8, 2026 – 5:34 AM Have you sorted your eclipse glasses yet?

Sunglasses are vital to safely view the partial stages of a solar eclipse. (Image credit: Photo by Gabriel BOUYS / AFP via Getty Images) If you'll be looking at any part of the partial eclipse, you'll need proper eye protection. Never look directly at the sun without certified eye protection.

Don't have eclipse glasses ? You can still safely enjoy the eclipse using simple projection methods with everyday household objects .

Check out our how to view the sun safely and what to look for guide for more solar viewing inspiration.

August 9, 2026 – 5:29 AM What actually happens during a total solar eclipse?

A composite image revealing the beauty of each stage surrounding totality. (Image credit: Photo by: Alan Dyer/VW Pics/UIG via Getty Images) Totality lasts only a few minutes, but a lot is happening before, during and after.

From first contact and the dramatic diamond ring effect to the appearance of the sun's corona, each stage offers something unique.
